open_points.subject: functions.add_trial_case input and expectation set
open_points.text: “input values by port, optional expected outputs”
open_points.question: Must inputs contain exactly every contract input and no extra names, and, when expected_outputs is present, must it contain exactly every contract output rather than a partial expectation?
options: Inputs are exact; expected_outputs is either absent or an exact complete output set
Reject missing inputs but ignore extra input or output names
Allow expected_outputs to contain only the outputs the case wants compared
open_points.default_guess: Require exactly all inputs, reject extras, and make expected_outputs either wholly absent or complete.

open_points.subject: bindings.check_installed_instances manifest validation
open_points.text: “a manifest record that cannot be read or fails a check of the record itself (A08 rule 5) stops the start naming it”
open_points.question: Which A08 rule 5 checks apply at startup when this operation has no operation name or proposed ports with which to perform the operation-specific checks?
options: Check only generic service-record structure and duplicate capability names, plus the selected instance facts needed for header collision
Validate every capability entry in the service record as though each were being proposed
Check only that the record can be parsed and the selected instance can be inspected
open_points.default_guess: Apply only record-wide structural checks and the selected-instance checks needed by this startup operation.

open_points.subject: sandbox.probe_sandbox
open_points.text: “bubblewrap is present and one probe execution succeeds”
open_points.question: What exact code, inputs, bounds, mounts and assertions constitute the probe, and which sandbox facilities must it exercise before startup succeeds?
options: Run a fixed trivial function through the full execute_function path
Exercise every namespace, trap and resource-limit mechanism
Only verify that bubblewrap launches the pinned interpreter
open_points.default_guess: Run a fixed release-defined trivial function through the same isolation and cleanup path used by execute_function.

open_points.subject: store.record_change integrity checks
open_points.text: “store checks only its own invariants — attempt numbers, unique and existing identities, links”
open_points.question: What exact links and referential constraints must each named change validate, and which violations are refused versus internal_error?
options: Validate only structural foreign-key existence and the explicitly stated attempt-number rules
Validate every cross-record relationship represented in the payload
Trust callers for all links and enforce only database uniqueness
open_points.default_guess: Validate structural referential integrity, immutable-record uniqueness and attempt-number consistency; treat caller-semantic inconsistencies as internal_error.

open_points.subject: store.record_change ordinal refusal propagation
open_points.text: “Errors: refused when an outcome's attempt is no longer the element's next ordinal” and “Between modules, a refusal is the same pair ... module:surface returns it unchanged”
open_points.question: When this store refusal reaches functions or runs, which do not define a conversion for it, is it exposed to the MCP caller as refused, converted to internal_error and followed by process shutdown, or declared unreachable?
options: Expose refused unchanged
Convert it to internal_error because it signals an invariant failure
Declare the condition unreachable and remove it from the public error contract
open_points.default_guess: Convert it to internal_error and stop after responding, because a single-writer correct caller cannot legitimately encounter it.

open_points.subject: effects.operation_element_conclusion data source
open_points.text: “waiting with its reason and, for owner_approval, the approval_id of the element's requested approval” and “Read from the NodeExecution and EffectAttempt together”
open_points.question: May this operation also read EffectApproval records, and what precedence determines the conclusion when an element has several historical executions, attempts and approvals?
options: Use the latest concluded attempt plus the currently requested approval, reading all three record types
Derive the conclusion only from NodeExecution and EffectAttempt and have runs supply the approval id
Treat any combination requiring an approval lookup as internal inconsistency
open_points.default_guess: Read NodeExecutions, EffectAttempts and EffectApprovals; derive from the latest attempt state and the one current requested approval.

open_points.subject: run answer contents
open_points.text: “A run's answer ... holds: run_id, the flow version, status, starter and times, outputs produced, waiting points ...”
open_points.question: Does the run answer also expose the Run model's inputs, pinned_implementations, resumptions and cancelled_by, or is the quoted list exhaustive?
options: Return the full M19 inspection data plus the derived output reasons
Return only the fields explicitly listed for the run answer
Return full M19 data only from get_run, but the smaller answer from mutating run operations and list_records
open_points.default_guess: Return the full M19 inspection data, masked for the reader, plus the derived output reasons.

open_points.subject: get_repair_view response
open_points.text: “functions.read_slot; the current contract version through functions.read_contract_version and its whole corpus; the current implementation ...”
open_points.question: Is the whole-history result of functions.read_slot returned to the caller, or is it used only internally while the repair view returns the current contract, current implementation, current corpus and recent executions required by K-12?
options: Return only the current repair context; use slot history internally to select traces
Return the whole slot history together with the current repair context
Return different scopes to the owner and an agent
open_points.default_guess: Use the history internally and return only the current repair context plus the specified recent executions.

open_points.subject: historical FlowActivation references
open_points.text: “flow activations through get_flow” while get_flow returns “its active version and FlowActivation”
open_points.question: How can a caller inspect the historical FlowActivation named as a draft-write EffectAttempt's authority after another activation has replaced it?
options: Embed the referenced FlowActivation in the EffectAttempt answer
Provide lookup or listing by the FlowActivation's store position
Leave the authority as an opaque, non-resolvable store position
open_points.default_guess: Return the referenced FlowActivation with the EffectAttempt inspection result.

open_points.subject: agent masking of many-file personal data
open_points.text: “The same holds for a personal_data file: an agent gets its digest and class”
open_points.question: What does an agent receive for a personal_data value on a many file port, where the durable representation is an ordered list of SpooledFiles and no aggregate file-list digest is defined?
options: An ordered list of per-file digest-and-class pairs
One aggregate digest and class for the entire list
Only the class, withholding the list length and all individual digests
open_points.default_guess: Return the ordered list of per-file digest-and-class pairs, preserving repetitions.

open_points.subject: masked failure_detail length
open_points.text: “a classified failure_detail its length and class”
open_points.question: Is the disclosed length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode code points, or another unit?
options: UTF-8 byte length
Unicode code-point count
Character count after replacement and truncation
open_points.default_guess: Use UTF-8 byte length, matching failure_detail_bytes_max.
